newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-F.A. LAUNCH INQUIRY AFTER BRISTOL PITCH INVASION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-F.A. LAUNCH INQUIRY AFTER BRISTOL PITCH INVASION.

text.p: The English Football Association launched an immediate inquiry after the Bristol derby between English second division sides City and Rovers ended in mayhem on Sunday.
Rovers fans staged a pitch invasion when their side scored and home supporters chased the Rovers players off the pitch after the final whistle.
The trouble started when Rovers equalised in injury time.
About 50 jubilant fans spilled on to the pitch at City's Ashton Gate ground and had to be restrained by police. Play was halted for five minutes while order was restored.

After the final seconds had been played, about 100 City fans stormed the pitch and chased the Rovers' players towards the changing rooms. Two players were trapped in a corner of the ground and had to be escorted to the tunnel by stewards.
The match, played in front of 18,674 fans, ended 1-1.
"It was a typical derby game but events have been overtaken by what happpened after the game," City manager Joe Jordan said. "It's disgraceful... a lot of people have let us down today."
